capabilities.target: idp.reset_mfa (remove a user's MFA methods and issue a temporary pass)
chat.send_temp_pass posts the temporary pass to the requester

inputs.source: Support tickets, including tickets emailed in by contractors

instructions.note: The prompt states that every reset needs analyst approval, but no structural control is declared for temporary pass delivery to the requester.

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval in the queue tool
controls.decay_rationale: Raw-action human approval is structurally outside the model, but effectiveness degrades under autonomy increase or approval fatigue from very high request volume.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to account owner record for temporary pass delivery
Human approval gate on temporary pass delivery

findings.title: Confused deputy and credential recovery takeover: untrusted ticket can trigger MFA reset for a target account and send the temporary pass to the requester

attack_path.note: Contractors and vendors can open tickets by email; requester is the email sender.
Agent can look up the target user profile and memberships.
Reset is gated by analyst approval that shows target account, requester, and full ticket text.
Temporary pass is sent to whoever opened the ticket, not to the account owner.

evidence.observation: The prompt directs the agent to look up the user, reset MFA, and send the temporary access pass to the person who opened the ticket.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, and the requester field is the email sender; the temporary pass goes to whoever opened the ticket, not to the account owner.
The analyst sees the exact target account, the requester, and the full ticket body before approving the MFA reset.
Two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift and most are routine, which raises approval-fatigue risk.

recommendations.action: Bind temporary pass delivery to the account owner's system-of-record contact channel instead of the ticket requester.
Add a separate raw-action approval gate for temporary pass delivery, including recipient and delivery channel, not only for MFA reset.
Rate-limit or step-up review for account recovery requests from external requester domains and for mismatches between requester and target account owner.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval gate removed or narrowed; approvals per reviewer per day rise further; median steps per task increases.

findings.title: Summary-gated irreversible recovery action avoided today, but raw-action reset approval still leaves pass delivery ungated and forecast worsens if the reset gate is removed

attack_path.note: Untrusted ticket content can request reset of another user's MFA.
Reset currently requires analyst raw-action approval.
After reset, pass is posted to the requester.

evidence.observation: The approval view is raw action, showing the exact target account, requester, and full ticket text rather than a model summary.
Analysts approve about 400 requests per shift, so the control is structurally independent but exposed to fatigue under increased autonomy or volume.
The pass is delivered to the requester, so the irreversible disclosure sink remains unapproved.

recommendations.action: Require explicit analyst approval of recipient and delivery channel for temporary passes, using the same raw-action queue style as reset approval.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval gate removed, narrowed, or approval volume per analyst increases enough that reset requests are routinely rubber-stamped.

rating.rationale: Untrusted emailed tickets can influence directory lookup, MFA reset, and delivery of a temporary pass to the requester. The declared raw-action analyst approval gate covers only cap.mfa_reset and does not sever the end-to-end recovery takeover path because cap.send_temp_pass remains reachable and is explicitly directed to the requester. Manual validation only; scripts were not available.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest, source code, or IdP/chat integration configuration was provided, so credential scope and exact enforcement points are taken as declared.
No runtime telemetry or queue audit samples were provided, so approval-fatigue impact is inferred from the stated volume rather than observed reviewer error rates.
